sermon.title: Four Difficult Issues to Understand Part 1
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer begins a look at four difficult issues in Revelation 20: the bottomless pit, Satan bound and loosed, the thousand years, and the first resurrection. He first questions the pre-tribulation rapture picture, then shows from Luke, Romans and Revelation what the bottomless pit is. He argues that Satan has been bound and loosed before, citing 1 Chronicles 21, Job and Luke 10, and that Satan was cast out of the earth when Jesus was lifted up.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: he says “Revelations” for the book of Revelation and the captions give “Revelations 9911,” which is Revelation 9:11. He cites “John 16:1” for the Holy Spirit convicting of sin, righteousness and judgment; those words are in John 16:8–11, which is shown. He uses King James wording (“bottomless pit,” “lightning fall from heaven”) where the NKJV reads “abyss” in Luke 8:31 and Romans 10:7; his words are unchanged. He says “Joel” was captioned for Job once; this is shown as Job. He makes claims about science (relativity, gravity, black holes) and about end-time doctrine; these are his words, not verified by this site. “[Unclear]” marks three spots in his story about a dam outlet (about 3:39–4:30) and one near the Job section (about 18:10).

chunks.short_answer: He says in Job that Satan could not touch Job because God had a hedge, and “Satan cannot do this till God gave permission.” He says God “will never let Satan or anything tempt you above what you can endure,” and “He doesn’t always remove it, but he empowers me to handle it.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Now there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan also came among them. And the LORD said to Satan, “From where do you come?” So Satan answered the LORD and said, “From going to and fro on the earth, and from walking back and forth on it.” Then the LORD said to Satan, “Have you considered My servant Job, that there is none like him on the earth, a blameless and upright man, one who fears God and shuns evil?” So Satan answered the LORD and said, “Does Job fear God for nothing? Have You not made a hedge around him, around his household, and around all that he has on every side? You have blessed the work of his hands, and his possessions have increased in the land. But now, stretch out Your hand and touch all that he has, and he will surely curse You to Your face!” And the LORD said to Satan, “Behold, all that he has is in your power; only do not lay a hand on his person.” So Satan went out from the presence of the LORD.

So Satan answered the LORD and said, “Skin for skin! Yes, all that a man has he will give for his life. But stretch out Your hand now, and touch his bone and his flesh, and he will surely curse You to Your face!” And the LORD said to Satan, “Behold, he is in your hand, but spare his life.” So Satan went out from the presence of the LORD, and struck Job with painful boils from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head.

No temptation has overtaken you except such as is common to man; but God is faithful, who will not allow you to be tempted beyond what you are able, but with the temptation will also make the way of escape, that you may be able to bear it.

chunks.section_question: What does Luke 10:18 teach about Satan’s fall and our authority?
chunks.short_answer: He reads “I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven” and says it happened “when these apostles went out and used the power of his word.” He says this is the first record that the apostles, and all believers, have authority over Satan.
chunks.text: Satan being cast out of heaven. “I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven.” See, the apostles went out and they preached the gospel, and they healed the sick, demons were cast out, people were saved, and they came back reporting to Jesus, and Jesus said, “I saw Satan as lightning fall from heaven” when, when these apostles went out and used the power of his word. “I give you power to tread on serpents and scorpions and over all the power of the enemy.” This is our first record that not only did the apostles have authority over Satan, but all of us believers have authority over

scriptures.text_nkjv: And He said to them, “I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven. Behold, I give you the authority to trample on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing shall by any means hurt you.

chunks.section_question: When does he say Satan was judged and cast out of the earth?
chunks.short_answer: He cites Revelation 12:7 and John 12:31, and says Satan was judged “when Jesus died on the cross.” He says “Satan was loose, now he’s bound,” that “You are a conqueror in the mess,” and that Satan “can do nothing without the big guy’s permission.”
chunks.text:
Satan. Hallelujah. It’s important for you to know this. See, so not only was he cast out, he was cast out by the preaching of God’s word from believers. Revelations 12:7, “War broke out in heaven, Michael and his angels fought with the dragon and his angels, that old great serpent, the great dragon, the serpent, the Devil.” Satan was cast out of heaven to the earth, and so, see, we have another, before the end of the world, when we, in, in Revelations 20, we have an account that Satan’s been cast down before. Amen. From heaven. John 12:31, we’re going to show you Scriptures where he was cast out of the earth. Okay, cast down from heaven to, to earth, now he’s cast out of the earth. “Now is the judgment of this world, now shall the prince of this world be cast out, and if I be lifted up from the earth I will draw all men to,” who? Me. So when was Satan judged and cast out of the earth? When Jesus died on the cross, when he was lifted up to draw all men to him, he cast the prince of this world

out. See, Satan was loose, now he’s bound. Are you there? See, it’s important for you to know that these things have been going on through the Bible. It’s very important, because this gives you the knowledge to live powerfully for Jesus Christ right now on earth. You’re not waiting for some, you know, magical thing at the end of the world to get you out of this mess. You are a conqueror in the mess. That’s right. That’s how powerful the blood, the cross, is. Again, in John 16:1, talking about the Holy Spirit that was going to come and convict us of sin, of righteousness, and of judgment, and he explains them. When he comes, to the judgment, he says, “of judgment because the prince of this world is” what? Judged. He sentenced, and we found in the Scripture before what was his sentence: he was cast out of the earth, so he couldn’t deceive

people. You say, “Well, you’re in trouble, because he’s still doing, well...” We’ll get there, we’ll get there. Remember, he’s been bound and loosed all throughout the Bible. Hallelujah. He can do nothing without the big guy’s permission.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And war broke out in heaven: Michael and his angels fought with the dragon; and the dragon and his angels fought, but they did not prevail, nor was a place found for them in heaven any longer. So the great dragon was cast out, that serpent of old, called the Devil and Satan, who deceives the whole world; he was cast to the earth, and his angels were cast out with him.
Now is the judgment of this world; now the ruler of this world will be cast out. And I, if I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all peoples to Myself.”

And when He has come, He will convict the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment: of sin, because they do not believe in Me; of righteousness, because I go to My Father and you see Me no more; of judgment, because the ruler of this world is judged.

faqs.question: What does he say the sword out of Jesus’s mouth is?
faqs.answer: He says “the sword that came out of Jesus’s mouth was what? The word of God.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Now out of His mouth goes a sharp sword, that with it He should strike the nations. And He Himself will rule them with a rod of iron. He Himself treads the winepress of the fierceness and wrath of Almighty God.

faqs.question: Why does he say God does not chain Satan with natural things?
faqs.answer: He says “God doesn’t use natural things to chain, he just uses his word. When he speaks, you can’t move.” The chain is given “so we understand in the natural, uh, in the spiritual what happens.”

faqs.question: What does he say darkness is?
faqs.answer: He says “darkness is the absence of light. There is no thing, such thing as darkness,” and “Light is its own character.”

faqs.question: What does he say about real photos of black holes?
faqs.answer: He says “when they really show a real photo of a black hole, there’s no black hole at all, there’s actually light there.”

faqs.question: What does he say happened to the demons in Luke 8?
faqs.answer: He says Jesus put them in a herd of pigs and “the pigs went nuts and ran down the cliff.” He says the demons asked not to be cast into the bottomless pit.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And they begged Him that He would not command them to go out into the abyss.

faqs.question: Who does he say is the king of the bottomless pit?
faqs.answer: He says the angel king called Apollyon, or Destroyer, “is Satan himself, he’s the king of the bottomless pit.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: And they had as king over them the angel of the bottomless pit, whose name in Hebrew is Abaddon, but in Greek he has the name Apollyon.

faqs.question: Why does he say people put wings on angels?
faqs.answer: He says “we put angels with wings on our Christmas trees, and we just do things because it’s handed down to us, and we don’t even think about what is the real source here.”

faqs.question: Why does he say God let Satan move David to number Israel?
faqs.answer: He says it was “God needing to deal with Israel because of their sins,” and that God “wants you to repent, turn, and live and do right.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Again the anger of the LORD was aroused against Israel, and He moved David against them to say, “Go, number Israel and Judah.”

faqs.question: Does he say God will let Satan tempt me beyond what I can bear?
faqs.answer: No. He says “He will never let Satan or anything tempt you above what you can endure. If you fall, it was your decision.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: No temptation has overtaken you except such as is common to man; but God is faithful, who will not allow you to be tempted beyond what you are able, but with the temptation will also make the way of escape, that you may be able to bear it.

faqs.question: What does he say happened to Job’s body?
faqs.answer: He says “Satan could not touch his body personally until God says you can,” and that “still Job would not denounce God.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: So Satan answered the LORD and said, “Skin for skin! Yes, all that a man has he will give for his life. But stretch out Your hand now, and touch his bone and his flesh, and he will surely curse You to Your face!” And the LORD said to Satan, “Behold, he is in your hand, but spare his life.” So Satan went out from the presence of the LORD, and struck Job with painful boils from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head.

faqs.question: Does he say we have to wait for the end of the world to be free?
faqs.answer: No. He says “You’re not waiting for some, you know, magical thing at the end of the world to get you out of this mess. You are a conqueror in the mess.”

faqs.question: What does he say the Holy Spirit convicts of?
faqs.answer: He says the Holy Spirit would “convict us of sin, of righteousness, and of judgment,” and the judgment is “because the prince of this world is” judged.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And when He has come, He will convict the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment: of sin, because they do not believe in Me; of righteousness, because I go to My Father and you see Me no more; of judgment, because the ruler of this world is judged.
